cycle_position.summary: Deep bifurcation. CBD office took a ~50% peak-to-trough price decline vs ~19% for suburban; CBD vacancy will fall more slowly for several more quarters (bigger pipelines, more space shedding). Some CBD trades print 400+ bps above 2019 caps (San Francisco CBD example: 9.6% vs 5.4% five years earlier). Medical office is the resilient corner: 9.8% vacancy, record rents, record retention.

cap_rate_ranges.note: Full observed Q1 2026 range 5.5%-8.5% by quality/tenancy; MOB trades 100-300 bps inside generic office.

supply_demand.value: CBD pipelines still delivering into weak demand; MOB pipelines near empty ('full waiting rooms, empty pipelines').

debt_terms.value: Bank CRE appetite for office remains the tightest of the majors; no primary terms captured this pass.

small_investor_verdict.entry_vehicle: Only the medical-office edge: a small suburban MOB or medical condo near a hospital cluster can fit $1-2M, at 6.5-8% caps with sticky tenants. Generic office — even cheap — is a leasing-capital trap at this scale.
small_investor_verdict.reasoning: TI/LC costs and re-leasing risk on small office suites consume the yield premium; the buyer's hands-on advantage doesn't transfer (tenant rep brokers gate deal flow). MOB's structural demand story is real but entry inventory at $1-2M is thin and often condo-form with association drag.

gaps: East Coast small-MOB inventory and pricing at the $1-2M ticket
Office-to-residential conversion economics for small buildings (relevant to the buyer's rowhouse markets; not researched)
